newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-March 18.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch-March 18.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Tuesday morning:
** Finance Minister P. Chidambaram told India's central bank on Monday that interest rates should be reduced to support economic growth.

Chidambaram told Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor C. Rangarajan that the annual inflation rate should be kept at six to seven percent to provide economic and political stability, the RBI said in a statement released in the capital.
** Quantitative restrictions on the import of consumer goods will be phased out and the sector opened in a few years, the Economic Times quoted the finance secretary as saying.

The paper quoted the finance secretary as saying it was logical for companies to increase their competitiveness and face international competition by having mergers, but distinctions should be made between mergers which encouraged competition and mergers which discouraged it.

** Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) plans to merge all its subsidiaries over the next three years to form a universal bank, the Business Standard quoted its chief executive officer as saying.
Imminent regulatory changes were expected to enable ICICI to knit its subsidiaries into a major financial monolith, it says.
** The Indian rupee opened steady at 35.8750/8850 on Tuesday, dealers said. Tuesday's range is seen at 35.86/89 rupees to a dollar.
The market looks to the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), whose dollar buying has been the key factor influencing the market.
** The benchmark 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange rose 52.81 points, or 1.41 percent, to end at 3,798.12.
** The National Stock Exchange index gained 2.50 points to 1,072.60.
** The Delhi share index was up 14.23 points to 789.93.
** The Madras share index climbed 6.37 points to 3,950.36.
** Travel and leisure firm, Thomas Cook India on Monday said it would offer shareholders two bonus shares for every three shares held.
The company said its net profit in the year ending December 1996 rose 25.6 percent to 136.5 million rupees against 108.6 million in the previous year.
